title: CSRF on sku_add.php - Missing CSRF Token Validation on POST Operations
impact:
CSRF attacks on sku_add.php can result in:
- Unauthorized creation of SKU records with attacker-controlled data
- Data pollution and inventory corruption
- False/malicious product records added to system
- Potential XSS via description field if not properly escaped during rendering
- Disruption of inventory management systems
- Administrative overhead to clean up malicious records
- No audit trail showing which users performed unauthorized additions
evidence:
Source code analysis and POC demonstration:

1. sku_add.php - No CSRF token validation in POST handler:
   - No session token verification
   - No Referer/Origin header validation
   - No CSRF token field required or validated
   - Direct database INSERT on POST parameters

2. HTML POC (poc_csrf_sku_add_attack.html) created demonstrating:
   - Malicious HTML form that targets sku_add.php
   - Hidden form fields with attacker-controlled SKU data (sku=MALICIOUS_001, name=Malicious SKU Created by CSRF)
   - Automatic form submission when page is visited or button clicked
   - No CSRF token included in the form (matching the vulnerability)
   - Attack executes in authenticated user's browser context with their session cookie

3. Attack Vector Confirmation:
   - Any unauthenticated attacker can create the malicious HTML page
   - Any user visiting the page while logged into the vulnerable application is vulnerable
   - Browser automatically includes session cookies in cross-site POST request
   - sku_add.php accepts request without any validation
   - Unauthorized SKU record created successfully
